drafts.title: Property due diligence before a transaction
drafts.summary: A practical overview of the questions that help organize a review of property records and contractual risk.

sections.title: Define the transaction
sections.body: The information required for an acquisition, lease or development arrangement depends on the rights being acquired, the parties involved and the intended use. Defining the transaction helps establish a meaningful scope of review.

sections.title: Review the documentary record
sections.body: Ownership history, relevant conveyance documents, existing interests and available property records should be considered together. Gaps or inconsistencies in the record may require further investigation.

sections.title: Consider use and restrictions
sections.body: A property’s legal title and its permissible use are distinct questions. Planning restrictions, contractual obligations and other applicable requirements may affect whether the intended use can proceed.

sections.title: Translate findings into decisions
sections.body: The review can inform conditions precedent, contractual protections and requests for additional documents. The appropriate response depends on the facts, jurisdiction and allocation of risk between the parties.

drafts.title: Reading land use in its development context
drafts.summary: How planning designations, site conditions and commercial objectives interact in property development.

sections.title: Identify the relevant framework
sections.body: Planning controls are specific to a location and may operate at more than one level. The relevant plan, authority and applicable instruments should be identified before drawing conclusions about development potential.

sections.title: Distinguish use from feasibility
sections.body: A use that is permissible in principle may still depend on physical site conditions, access, infrastructure or development controls. Legal permissibility does not by itself establish practical or commercial feasibility.

sections.title: Consider the sequence of decisions
sections.body: Development may involve multiple decisions, documents and approvals. Understanding dependencies helps identify which questions need to be resolved before commitments are made.

sections.title: Keep the context current
sections.body: Planning instruments and their interpretation can change. A site-specific review should rely on the applicable current materials and the facts of the proposed development.

drafts.title: Questions to consider in joint development arrangements
drafts.summary: A framework for examining contributions, responsibilities and change in a development agreement.

sections.title: Establish the contributions
sections.body: A development arrangement may involve land, capital, technical expertise and project management. The agreement should make clear what each party is expected to contribute and when.

sections.title: Clarify obligations
sections.body: Responsibilities for documentation, approvals, financing and delivery need to be understood alongside the project’s commercial assumptions. Unclear dependencies can create difficulties as a project progresses.

sections.title: Consider changes and delays
sections.body: Development takes place over time, and costs, market conditions or project requirements may change. Mechanisms for variation, delay and decision-making can help the parties address uncertainty.

sections.title: Understand the exit framework
sections.body: The agreement should be reviewed in the context of completion, default, termination and dispute resolution. The relevance of particular provisions depends on the nature of the arrangement and applicable law.
